claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The as-built alloy has a fine FCC matrix, residual stresses, and characteristic additive-manufacturing microstructural features.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by a transition in oxidation behavior.
At moderate oxygen partial pressures, Al and Ti diffuse to form an Al/Ti-rich surface oxide scale.
The Al/Ti-rich oxide scale is continuous and protective, retarding further oxidation and preserving mechanical integrity.
Increasing oxygen activity beyond a critical threshold changes the dominant oxidation mode to rapid, localized grain-boundary oxidation.
Localized grain-boundary oxidation causes intergranular embrittlement, microcracking, and catastrophic failure.
Catastrophic degradation can follow severe high-temperature oxidation.
Under reducing atmospheres, a stabilizing external oxide scale does not form adequately.
Insufficient scale formation under reducing conditions permits internal oxidation.
Reducing conditions can cause phase decomposition in this alloy.
Internal oxidation and phase decomposition under reducing conditions promote microcrack initiation and accelerate failure.
Systematically varying oxygen partial pressure or the oxidizing-to-reducing gas ratio at constant temperature is the proposed controlled intervention.
At moderate oxygen partial pressure, a uniform continuous scale will delay degradation.
At higher oxygen partial pressure, discontinuous grain-boundary oxidation will coincide with reduced strength and earlier catastrophic failure.
Under reducing conditions, internal oxidation and phase changes will produce premature degradation relative to the as-built baseline.
In inert or low-oxygen atmospheres, the as-built material exhibits minimal oxidation-induced degradation.
The proposed oxidation-transition mechanism is applicable between 700 and 800 degrees Celsius.
The critical oxygen partial pressure and the kinetics of internal oxidation have not yet been quantitatively determined.

contradictions.description: The baseline assigns minimal oxidation-induced degradation to inert or low-oxygen atmospheres, while the mechanism and prediction assign internal oxidation and premature degradation to reducing atmospheres, which ordinarily also have low oxygen activity. The hypothesis does not specify gas chemistry or an oxygen-activity boundary that reconciles these statements.
